hero.eyebrow: Challenges with friends · Pot secured on Arbitrum
hero.title: Challenge your friends. The pot's already collected.
hero.subtitle: The pot exists before there's a winner. Everyone pays in when they join, into an Arbitrum contract written in Rust with Stylus, and the money can only go to the winner or back to whoever put it in.

product.subtitle: It happens in every pot between friends: two out of five will "pay you later". Today the pot is just a promise in the group chat, and chasing a friend for money is awkward. OtterPot collects it upfront.

blockchain.q: Do I need to know about blockchain?
blockchain.a: No. You create the challenge and deposit from Telegram; the technical part runs behind the scenes.

funds.q: Who holds the money during the challenge?
funds.a: Nobody: the contract controls it. It can only pay a participant of the challenge or refund each person what they put in. Neither the bot nor our team can send it anywhere else.

telegram.q: Can I use it from Telegram only?
telegram.a: Yes. You can create challenges, invite people and track progress from the bot and the Mini App.

noContract.q: What if the group can't agree?
noContract.a: If the deadline passes with no confirmed winner, the contract refunds everyone's deposit, with no fee.

cost.a: Creating an account is free. When a challenge is resolved, a fee is taken from the pot; refunds are fee-free.

footer.disclaimer: Testnet prototype (Arbitrum Sepolia): uses test USDC with no real value. While a challenge runs, the pot may be deposited in Aave to earn yield, which adds that protocol's risk. Next step: support for Paxos USDG.

feedback.title: What the judges say
feedback.subtitle: Reviews from the ETH Lima representatives who evaluated OtterPot, and what we did about each point.

antonella.quote: I liked that you can create a routine, save it, track it, earn rewards, connect your wallet and do different activities inside the app's challenges.
antonella.response: Today, progress is validated with evidence and a group vote. Automatic activity validation through Google Fit / Health Connect is on the roadmap.

gianella.quote: OtterPot's proposal stands out for solving a very real friction in groups: having to trust one person with the money. Bringing smart contracts directly into Telegram makes the experience accessible and natural, while configurable consensus and automatic refunds significantly reduce the risks. On top of that, connecting these social challenges with DeFi gives it interesting potential to bring new users into the Web3 ecosystem.
gianella.response: On DeFi: while the pot is locked it can earn yield, and that yield goes first toward covering the fee. Anything left over is a bonus for the winner.

alejandra.quote: The proposal is well focused and the use of blockchain is clearly justified: pot custody, resolution rules and refunds genuinely benefit from running without an intermediary. As an improvement, I'd revisit the consensus mechanism to prevent collusion or manipulation between participants and better explain what happens with ambiguous results. It would also be important to clearly communicate the risk of temporarily placing funds in Aave, since custody is no longer fully passive. Finally, the Stylus argument is interesting, but it should be backed by real gas metrics against an equivalent Solidity implementation. That would make the technical case for using Arbitrum much stronger.
alejandra.response: For ambiguous results: if the deadline passes without a majority, the contract refunds everyone with no fee. Against collusion, a designated-judge mode is on the roadmap. The Aave risk is now explained in the footer, and we're measuring Stylus gas against Solidity.

botGuide.title: How to use the bot
botGuide.subtitle: It all happens in your group chat. It takes less time than reading this.
botGuide.note: Deposits currently use test USDC (Arbitrum Sepolia).

find.title: Add the bot to your group
find.body: Open Telegram, search for {bot} and add it to the group you'll play in.

create.title: Type /nuevo
create.body: Set the amount and deadline. For example, /nuevo 25 24 sets up a 25 USDC challenge for 24 hours.

join.title: Everyone signs up
join.body: Participants tap "Me sumo" (I'm in). Once everyone's in, /abrir creates the challenge in the contract.

deposit.title: Everyone pays in
deposit.body: /depositar opens the Mini App, and each person signs their share from their own wallet.

confirm.title: The group confirms
confirm.body: When it's over, everyone votes for the winner with /confirmar @username.

payout.title: The contract pays out
payout.body: With a majority, the pot goes to the winner. If the deadline passes with no agreement, /reembolso gives everyone their money back.
